title: Your Money Just Got Safer: RBI Governor Pushes for Stronger Bank Security
description: RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das recently urged banks to boost their cybersecurity measures. This push comes as online financial frauds are becoming more common a.

faq.a: Cybersecurity in banking refers to the measures and technologies banks use to protect their computer systems, networks, and data from digital attacks, theft, or damage, ensuring the safety of your financial information and transactions.

faq.q: How does the RBI enforce these cybersecurity measures?
faq.a: The RBI issues guidelines, circulars, and mandates that banks must follow. It also conducts regular audits and inspections to ensure banks comply with these security standards and can impose penalties for non-compliance.

faq.q: What can I do to protect my money online?
faq.a: Always use strong, unique passwords, enable two-factor authentication, never share your OTP, PIN, or CVV with anyone, be wary of suspicious links or calls, and regularly check your bank statements for unusual activity.

faq.q: Will banks charge extra for these enhanced security features?
faq.a: Typically, banks absorb the costs of implementing these security upgrades as part of their operational expenses. These measures are fundamental to providing a safe banking service and are generally not passed on as direct charges to customers for basic security.

faq.q: What should I do if I suspect I've been a victim of online fraud?
faq.a: Immediately contact your bank's fraud department and block your cards. You should also file a complaint with the cybercrime cell by calling 1930 or visiting the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal.

fact_check.summary: The article is largely reliable, accurately reflecting the RBI's focus on cybersecurity and providing sound advice for customers. However, it incorrectly states the name of the current RBI Governor.
